chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed Allah — Blessed is His Name, and Exalted is His Mention, and Majestic is His Laudation. Glorified is He, and Holy, and Individual, and One. He did not cease to be and will not cease to be. And He is the First and the Last, and the Manifest and the Hidden.

So there is no first to His being First. Raised in His Highest Loftiness: Lofty of the Elements, Raiser of Structures, Magnificent of Authority, of High Eminence, Sublime Highness — He before Whom the describers are unable to describe His Essence, nor can they endure bearing recognition of His Divinity, nor can they reach His limits, because He, through qualitative states, cannot be reached.

key_terms.إِلَهِيَّتِهِ: His God-ness/Divinity — the reality of His being God
key_terms.الْأَوَّلُ وَالْآخِرُ وَالظَّاهِرُ وَالْ: The First, the Last, the Manifest, the Hidden — the four Names of God from Quran 57:3
key_terms.بِالْكَيْفِيَّةِ لَا يُتَنَاهَى: Through qualitative states, cannot be reached — God transcends all categorical description
key_terms.تَبَارَكَ اسْمُهُ: Blessed is His Name — an honorific title for God
key_terms.سُبْحَانَهُ: Glorified is He — technical term for God's absolute purity
key_terms.كُنْهِ صِفَتِهِ: The essence/reality of His attribute — God's inner nature beyond all descriptions

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the transcendence and attributes of Allah in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith is narrated by Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) and forms part of Chapter 22 of Usul al-Kafi, which is devoted to comprehensive statements about Divine Oneness (Tawhid). The Imam opens with a series of divine glorifications — Blessed Name, Exalted Mention, Majestic Praise — building to the transcendent Names al-Awwal (First), al-Akhir (Last), al-Zahir (Manifest), al-Batin (Hidden), which are also Quranic Names of God (57:3). The climax of the teaching is the radical transcendence of God: not only are describers unable to reach His essence, they cannot even bear to comprehend His divinity, because He transcends all qualitative categories.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Salih Bin Abu Hammad, from Al Husayn Bin Yazed, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Ibrahim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Blessed is His<sup>azwj</sup> Name, and Exalted is His<sup>azwj</sup> Mention, and Majestic is His<sup>azwj</sup> Laudation. Glorious is He<sup>azwj</sup>, and Holy, and Individual, and Unique, and He<sup>azwj</sup> did not Cease to be and will not Cease to be, and He<sup>azwj</sup> is the First, and the Last, and the Manifest, and the Hidden.

So there is no first to His<sup>azwj</sup> being First, Raised in His<sup>azwj</sup> High Loftiness. Lofty of the elements, Raiser of the Structures, Magnificent of the Authority, of High Eminence, Sublime Highness which the describers are unable from describing His<sup>azwj</sup> Essence, nor are they enduring the bearing of recognising His<sup>azwj</sup> God-ness, nor are they reaching its limits, because He<sup>azwj</sup>, by the qualitative states, cannot be reached.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Salih ibn Hammad from al-Husayn ibn Yazid from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn abu Hamza from Ibrahim from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) Who has said the following.

“Allah, the Most Holy is Whose name, the Most High is Whose praise, the Most Glorious are Whose attributes. He is the Most Sacred, the Most Holy, the only One in oneness. He is eternal, the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden.

There is no beginning for Him. He is the Most Exalted in His highness. The Highest in power, Exalted in authority, the greatest in kingdom, the Most bountiful, His Highness is the Most High. He is the One whose praise no one can complete, and can not bear the knowledge of His Lordship. No one is able to limit Him because it is not possible to reach Him with qualities.”
